transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. I'm here to help you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've been having these constant, intrusive memories of a traumatic event that happened two weeks ago. Sometimes it feels like I’m actually reliving it all over again, and I just can't seem to get those images out of my head.
I am sorry you are going through this. To help me understand better, has this traumatic event occurred within the past month, or has it been going on for longer than that?
It happened exactly two weeks ago. I have been struggling with these memories every single day since then.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports that the traumatic event occurred only two weeks ago. According to the DSM-5-TR, a diagnosis of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder requires symptoms to persist for more than one month, whereas Acute Stress Disorder is diagnosed when symptoms are present for three days to one month following exposure to a traumatic event. Given the two-week timeframe, the clinical presentation is consistent with Acute Stress Disorder.
